short: Enhanced electromagnetic wave absorption property of binary
title: Enhanced electromagnetic wave absorption property of binary ZnO/NiCo2O4 composites

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Microwave absorbers need strong loss together with impedance matching; single-component oxides give one or the other. A binary ZnO/NiCo2O4 hybrid should add heterointerfaces whose interfacial polarisation raises dielectric loss and so the absorption.
states.detail: Absorbed: c1 (HYP/need), c2 (HYP/hypothesis), c3 (DES/base_system), c4 (DES/modification), c5 (DES/variable_sweep), c6 (PRC/synthesis), c7 (PRC/synthesis)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Two phases only: hexagonal ZnO (PDF 99-0111) and spinel NiCo2O4 (PDF 20-0781), no impurity phase in any sample. NiCo2O4 nano-dots sit in direct lattice contact with the ZnO, giving a dense array of ZnO/NiCo2O4 heterointerfaces inside each aggregate.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Complex permittivity rises with NH3.H2O content: maximum real part 5.78, 6.85, 6.96 and imaginary part about 0.33, 0.48, 0.67 at 18 GHz. The powders are essentially non-magnetic (Ms 0.0007 emu/g, Hc 60 Oe), so magnetic loss is argued to play little part.
states.detail: Absorbed: c13 (PRP/value), c14 (PRP/value), c15 (PRP/value), c16 (MEC/pathway), c18 (PRP/value). Premises: ZnO is a non-magnetic semiconductor and NiCo2O4 is non-magnetic at room temperature; Transmission-line theory gives the reflection loss from the complex parameters and thickness; matching is judged by |delta| < 0.4 and dissipation by the attenuation constant

states.title: Performance state
states.head: ZnO/NiCo2O4-7 absorbs best: minimum reflection loss -33.49 dB at 18.0 GHz and 4.99 mm, against -27.46 dB for -10 and only -6.52 dB for -5
states.detail: Absorbed: c19 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: Transmission-line theory gives the reflection loss from the complex parameters and thickness; matching is judged by |delta| < 0.4 and dissipation by the attenuation constant

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: A binary ZnO/NiCo2O4 hybrid tuned by alkalinity gives a purely dielectric Ku-band absorber reaching -33.49 dB

nodes.title: DERIVED, TRANSPORT:VNA, F5, F7
nodes.head: The dielectric loss tangent is highest for -10 at every frequency (about 0.10 at 18 GHz); -7 reaches only about 0.07 and is overtaken by -5 between 10 and 13 GHz. The attenuation constant rises with frequency for all three and ranks -10 (about 84) above -7 (about 73) above -5 (about 55) at 18 GHz
nodes.solves: Dielectric loss tangent and attenuation constant both rise with NH3.H2O content and with frequency, reaching alpha about 84, 73 and 55 at 18 GHz for -10, -7 and -5
nodes.note: so the best absorber (-7) is not the sample with the highest dielectric loss tangent, contrary to the record's summary

nodes.head: The Cole-Cole loci carry three labelled segments I, II and III per sample, but are dominated by a near-vertical rise of the imaginary part at almost constant real part

10.1007/s40145-021-0476-z#F1b.definition: SEM images of the as-obtained samples $\mathrm { Z n O / N i C o _ { 2 } O _ { 4 } \mathrm { - } }$ 5
use: Figures 1(b)–1(d) demonstrate the morphologies of the as-obtained powders observed by SEM.

As shown in Fig. 1, both the $\mathrm { Z n O / N i C o } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } _ { 4 } { - } 5$ and $\mathrm { Z n O / N i C o _ { 2 } O _ { 4 } } – \mathrm { 7 }$ samples are irregular shape particles ranging from several nanometers to hundred nanometers (Figs. 1(b) and 1(c)).

10.1007/s40145-021-0476-z#F1d.definition: SEM images of the as-obtained samples $\mathrm { Z n O / N i C o _ { 2 } O _ { 4 } } \mathrm { - } 1 0$
use: The SEM image of $\mathrm { Z n O / N i C o _ { 2 } O _ { 4 } } \mathrm { - } 1 0$ apparently represents a wellregulated structure (Fig. 1(d)).

As seen from Fig. 2(b), the lattice plane of the main phase is about $0 . 2 6 \ \mathrm { n m }$ corresponding to (002) lattice type plane in hexagonal structure of $Z _ { \mathrm { { n O } } }$ $( P 6 3 m c )$ .
The lattice space of the nano-dot is about $0 . 2 3 ~ \mathrm { n m }$ (Fig. 2(c)), consistent with the distance of (222) plane of the $\mathrm { N i C o } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } _ { 4 }$ .
The phase and crystal structure of the as-obtained powders are analyzed by XRD and the results are shown in Fig. 1(a).
The surface-scanning element mapping (Fig. 2(d)) clearly demonstrates the distribution of elements.

From Figs. 5(a) and 5(b), it can be seen that both the real $( \varepsilon ^ { \prime } )$ and imaginary $( \varepsilon ^ { \prime \prime } )$ parts of the permittivity increase with increasing the $\mathrm { N H } _ { 3 } { \cdot } \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O }$ content.
Figure 5(c) represents the dielectric loss tangent $( \varepsilon ^ { \prime \prime } / \varepsilon ^ { \prime } )$ of the synthesized samples.

10.1007/s40145-021-0476-z#F7d.definition: $\alpha$ values of $\mathrm { Z n O / N i C o _ { 2 } O _ { 4 } }$ samples

use: Figures 5(d) and 5(e) show the real $( \mu )$ and imaginary parts $( \mu ^ { \prime \prime } )$ of complex permeability of the $\mathrm { Z n O / N i C o _ { 2 } O _ { 4 } }$ samples.
As shown in Figs. 5(e) and 5(f), some resonance peaks are found for the three samples.

As it can be seen from Fig. 6(a), the $C _ { 0 }$ values of the $\mathrm { Z n O / N i C o _ { 2 } O _ { 4 } }$ samples gradually decrease within the frequency range of $2 . 0 { - } 1 8 . 0 \mathrm { G H z }$ , suggesting that eddy current effect has no contribution for the magnetic energy loss in this range.
